Every level/wave plays out the same across every map, every gamemode, and even when the special enemies come into play.
You don't have to take my word for it, just look at the achievement stats: half the players who launched the game didn't even kill 100 zombies (literally a few minutes of gameplay), only 1 in 6 finished the first non-tutorial campaign, and only 1 in 10 finished the second non-tutorial campaign.
The later campaigns have completion rates around 1-2%, and not because they're any more difficult.

Also, the checkpoint system is incredibly bad: restarting from a checkpoint means restarting without any ammo, which for the later checkpoints guarantees you'll not be able to survive and will have to restart the campaign from scratch.

It's clearly a "co-op first" game, though.
The "moving/shooting makes your aim worse" mechanic works well and discourages tedious kiting and pillar dancing.
Plays well with a controller -- my one criticism is that "open door" on B makes it hard to open a door while aiming -- whereas manual reload (rarely needed) is on RB.

Suggestions for improvement.
Please make all weapons auto-reload on level transitions.  You can do this by hand, but it's a chore.
Some visual indication of weapon type and mag/ammo near the center of the screen would also not go amiss.  Often I blow through heavy bullets and switch to an auto weapon, and it takes half a second for me to realize I should switch to full-auto fire.  Maybe just change the color/shape of the targeting reticle?

Quick:
Good basics so far for early access, but no reason to keep playing the game. Recommend ONLY for people who would like an easy top down shooter to play with non-gamer friends. Lack of any complexity means nothing new, exciting, or fun is here for experienced gamers.

Video:
https://youtu.be/nr0SDt5IdsI

Long:
The gameplay revolves around clearing waves of zombies and surviving the next and next wave.
The game offers 7 maps a good mix for early access but each offer no environmental differences to use within the maps just making them different layouts rather then any changing feel or tactics.
You have 5 ammo types to use, quick one, powerful one so on, this adds decision making to the player about which ammo to use when but as they have gone for this approach rather then changing guns implies lazy programming and minimises the possible extremes of which can be offered through the gun system.
Zombies are an effective enough enemy, put aside the overuse, this means the many type of threat is from them getting close and it boils the game down to how well you can move back while shooting.
The game is early access and has a good skeleton currently but the fate of this game is going to revolve for me around innovation. What can the game add to make me want to keep playing because currently the game cycle is very repetitive, a good game if you have a few non gamer friends that you want to play an easy pick up shooter with then this is for you. For gamers I don't see anything here to appeal to you, suffering from one of the worst things that can be said of the game and that is boring, seeming not to risk interesting gameplay and sticking to a standard but lets see how the meat does between now and launch.

It's very early so lot of feature are basic but it got some decent work in it.
The game is pretty much shown in the trailer and demo.
Zombie Horde survival on cramped map with sonar radar and noise. You got different ammo type to help you in your fight
Rapid fire to quickly dispatch weak zombie or group, spread shot for the shotgun enthusiast, power and heavy shot to deal more damage.
The darkness coupled with the narrow field of view will keep you on your toe as you progress through the wave of zombie growing stronger.

Now for the downside.
•The map feel a bit too small, especially if you add more people.
•For now there's no visual difference with ammo type, you have a pistol that can support a wide variety of ammo (maybe in future it will change.) but each ammo type doesn't have a specific trail to help you or other know what you're using.
•You can't rebind the control BUT it support both qwerty and azerty, and it's not a big issue as you only need to move and shoot with the mouse, no fluff.
•The sonar radar seems a bit clunky it work and sometime it doesn't, so dont entirely rely on it to know where the zombie are.

But for 5$ game, it's quite good and well made and fun to play.
